answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before submitting jobs or claiming rewards. If reviewers find that accounts share control or collude, the protocol excludes them and burns part of their bonds. A plume of aliases cannot multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital per account and risks losing it when detected. Bonds do not prove uniqueness, and an island of unchecked accounts remains vulnerable; diverse reviewers can help spot a reef of coordinated fakes.
